by: the quality rules and auto-fixes that refuse the shortcut each architectural rule forbids
check.population: every source file under a governed root
check.freshness: a verdict stands until the source or the rule changes
check.refusal: a rule that fires fails the lint stage, and an auto-fix rewrites the shortcut where the fix is deterministic
check.observation: the telemetry a runtime rule requires, such as observed execution, which locates a path that runs unobserved
check.evidence: none: the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it
check.authority: the architectural rule, which the source conforms to and an auto-fix rewrites toward

records.title: Constraints Over Shortcuts
records.intent: Replace a debt-incurring shortcut with an encoded constraint that makes the invalid state unrepresentable, so the rule holds without relying on discipline.
records.invariant: A value that could be constructed invalidly is instead constructed only through a validating boundary.

records.title: Forward Compatibility Over Backward Compatibility
records.intent: Replace accreted legacy input shapes with one forward-compatible envelope that carries extensions, so evolution compounds instead of branching.
records.invariant: One canonical shape with an open extension slot subsumes every prior variant; no shape-discriminating branch remains.

records.title: Fail-Fast Over Fallback
records.intent: Replace a silent fallback default with a required input that halts loudly when absent, so missing configuration surfaces at the boundary.
records.invariant: Every required input is present and validated before use; absence throws rather than defaulting.

records.title: Explicit Removal Over Deprecation
records.intent: Replace a deprecated alias kept for compatibility with outright removal, so the single current name is the only path.
records.invariant: No symbol exists solely to forward to another; every callsite targets the canonical name.

records.title: Greenfield Over Legacy
records.intent: Replace a legacy-mode branch with one current algorithm, deleting the old path rather than gating it behind a flag.
records.invariant: A single implementation serves the concern; no legacy-mode conditional selects behavior.

records.title: Single-Path Determinism Over Dual-Path
records.intent: Collapse a flag-selected dual path into one deterministic path, removing the branch and the flag that caused ambiguity.
records.invariant: Exactly one code path handles the operation; no runtime flag chooses between equivalent implementations.

records.title: Immediacy Over Deferring
records.intent: Replace a deferred follow-up with an atomic action that completes every coupled effect now, so nothing is forgotten.
records.invariant: Coupled effects commit together within one boundary; no effect is left as an implicit later step.

records.title: Mandatory Over Optional
records.intent: Replace an optional dependency with a mandatory one, removing the null-guarded branch so behavior is system-defined not caller-defined.
records.invariant: A dependency the behavior relies on is always supplied; no optional-chaining guards its use.

records.title: Now Over For-Now
records.intent: Replace a temporary in-memory placeholder with the real durable implementation immediately, so the stopgap never ossifies.
records.invariant: State that must survive restarts is persisted through the real store, not a transient map.

records.title: Observed Execution Over Unobserved
records.intent: Wrap an unobserved effect in structured telemetry so every execution emits a learnable signal on success and failure.
records.invariant: Every significant effect opens and closes a span carrying its outcome; no path executes blind.

records.title: Compression Over Repetition
records.intent: Extract a repeated pattern into one parameterized form, so the behavior lives once and duplication cannot drift.
records.invariant: A behavior expressed more than once is factored to a single definition parameterized over its variation.

records.title: Approved Evolution Over Unapproved
records.intent: Gate a structural dependency behind a recorded architecture decision, so evolution proceeds only through approved boundaries.
records.invariant: Every cross-boundary dependency traces to an approved decision record naming the allowed gateway.

records.title: Enforced Feedback Over Ignored
records.intent: Turn a logged-and-ignored warning into an enforced result, so negative feedback changes control flow instead of scrolling past.
records.invariant: A detected invalid condition returns a typed failure; it is never merely logged and continued.

records.title: Single Owner Over Shared Ownership
records.intent: Give one service authority over a piece of state and propagate to others by event, removing multi-writer ambiguity.
records.invariant: Exactly one service mutates a given entity; peers react to its events rather than co-writing it.

records.title: Bounded Lifetime Over Unbounded
records.intent: Replace an unbounded cache with a capacity-bounded structure that evicts and clears, so memory release is deterministic.
records.invariant: Every retained collection has an explicit bound and an eviction policy; growth cannot be unlimited.

records.title: Enforced Symmetry Over Asymmetric Lifecycle
records.intent: Pair every acquire with a guaranteed release via try/finally, so a fault mid-use cannot leak the resource.
records.invariant: Acquisition and release are structurally symmetric; release runs on every exit path.

records.title: Explicit Retention Over Implicit
records.intent: Replace an anonymous listener push with an explicit retention token that names its owner and exposes release.
records.invariant: Every retained reference is held through an ownership token that can be observed and released.

records.title: Structural Release Over Discipline
records.intent: Replace manual release calls with a language disposal scope, so cleanup is enforced structurally, not by the developer's memory.
records.invariant: Resource cleanup is bound to scope exit by the language, not to a manually written release call.

records.title: Immutable Data Over Mutable State
records.intent: Replace in-place mutation with a pure transform returning new data, so state transitions are reproducible.
records.invariant: Data is readonly; a change produces a new value rather than mutating the existing one.

records.title: Errors As Language Over Silent Errors
records.intent: Replace a null-on-failure return with a typed result union, so failure is machine-processable rather than swallowed.
records.invariant: A fallible operation returns a discriminated ok/error result; failure carries a typed code.

records.title: Explicit Invalidity Over Hidden
records.intent: Model invalid state as an explicit variant rather than coercing to a plausible default that hides uncertainty.
records.invariant: Validity is a represented state; invalid inputs map to an invalid variant, never a silent valid default.

records.title: Event Emission Over Parent Callbacks
records.intent: Replace a parent-supplied callback with an emitted event, decoupling the producer from its consumers.
records.invariant: A component announces facts via events; it holds no reference to who reacts.

records.title: Monotonic Growth Over Retraction
records.intent: Replace destructive deletion with an append-only removal event, so history is monotonic and projectable.
records.invariant: State changes append events; nothing is deleted in place, and current state is a projection.

records.title: Semantic Addressing Over Location Addressing
records.intent: Replace positional path addressing with a semantic identity reference, so references survive structural change.
records.invariant: An entity is referenced by stable identity, never by its position within a container.

exemplar.before:
const foo = document.sections[2].items[4];
const reference = "sections[2].items[4]";

records.title: Ordinal Time Over Timestamps
records.intent: Replace wall-clock ordering with an ordinal sequence, so event order is logical and clock-independent.
records.invariant: Ordering derives from a monotonic ordinal, not a physical timestamp subject to skew.

records.title: Homoiconicity Over Separation
records.intent: Fuse behavior and its separate metadata into one homoiconic data structure that is both the rule and its description.
records.invariant: A rule is represented as data that is directly evaluated; no parallel metadata can drift from it.

records.title: Bounded Complexity Over Unlimited
records.intent: Constrain an open-ended rule surface to a bounded grammar with depth and fan-out limits, capping cognitive load.
records.invariant: A rule structure has enforced maximum depth and breadth; unbounded nesting is rejected.

records.title: Computed Health Over Metric Health
records.intent: Replace threshold-on-metrics health with a symbolic diagnosis that names the causes of an unready state.
records.invariant: Health is a computed state naming concrete blocking causes, not a boolean over numeric thresholds.

records.title: Secret Store Over Hardcoded Secrets
records.intent: Replace an inline secret with a resolved read from a secret store that fails fast when the secret is absent.
records.invariant: No secret literal appears in source; secrets are read at runtime from a store and validated present.

records.title: Boundary Validation Over Unvalidated Input
records.intent: Parse and validate untrusted input at the boundary into a typed shape, failing fast on malformed data.
records.invariant: Input crosses the boundary only after schema validation; no raw external value reaches the core.

records.title: Least Privilege Over Broad Privilege
records.intent: Narrow a broad capability to the minimal typed interface a task needs, shrinking the blast radius.
records.invariant: A component receives only the narrow capability its task requires, never an ambient broad authority.

records.title: Config Externalization Over Env Fallback
records.intent: Replace env-var-or-default reads with a validated config loaded at boot that fails fast on missing values.
records.invariant: Configuration is parsed and validated once at startup; a missing required var halts boot.

exemplar.before:
const fooUrl = process.env.FOO_URL || "http://localhost:3000";
const retryCount = Number(process.env.FOO_RETRIES || "3");

records.title: Profile-First Over Unmeasured Optimization
records.intent: Gate any optimization behind a measured profile, so effort is evidence-driven rather than speculative.
records.invariant: A performance change is justified by a before/after measurement of the actual bottleneck.

records.title: Rule As Code Over Convention
records.intent: Replace a written convention with an automated gate, so the invariant is enforced by code not by memory.
records.invariant: Every stated invariant has an executable check that fails the build on violation.

records.title: Design By Contract Over Implicit Contract
records.intent: State pre-conditions, post-conditions, and invariants explicitly, so a boundary's contract is checkable not assumed.
records.invariant: A boundary declares and enforces its pre/post/invariant conditions; callers are not left to guess.

records.title: Versioned Evolution Over Breaking Change
records.intent: Introduce change behind a version so existing consumers keep a stable contract while new ones adopt the new shape.
records.invariant: A contract change is additive or versioned; no in-place change breaks an existing consumer silently.

exemplar.before: app.get("/foo", () => ({ label: "Foo", tags: [] }));
exemplar.after:
app.get("/v1/foo", () => ({ name: "Foo" }));
app.get("/v2/foo", () => ({ label: "Foo", tags: [] }));

records.title: Schema-Validated Boundary Over Untyped
records.intent: Type and schema-validate every boundary crossing, so invalid state cannot enter the typed core.
records.invariant: Data entering the system is validated against a schema; untyped values never propagate inward.

records.title: Atomic Boundary Over Partial Commit
records.intent: Wrap coupled writes in an all-or-nothing boundary, so a fault cannot leave state half-applied.
records.invariant: Coupled state changes either all commit or all roll back; no partial application persists.

records.title: Saga Compensation Over Distributed 2PC
records.intent: Replace a cross-service two-phase commit with a saga of compensable steps, preserving service autonomy.
records.invariant: Cross-service consistency is achieved by compensating actions, not a distributed lock across services.

records.title: Async Events Over Synchronous Cross-Boundary
records.intent: Replace a synchronous call across an autonomy boundary with an asynchronous event, decoupling in time.
records.invariant: Calls across autonomy boundaries are asynchronous; no boundary blocks on another's synchronous response.

records.title: Observable Signals Over Opaque Runtime
records.intent: Emit structured signals around runtime behavior, so operation is observable rather than blind.
records.invariant: Runtime paths emit structured telemetry sufficient to reconstruct what happened.

records.title: Injected Dependency Over Hidden
records.intent: Surface a concealed dependency as a constructor parameter, inverting control and revealing coupling.
records.invariant: Every dependency is injected and visible in the signature; none is reached for ambiently.

records.title: Convention Discovery Over Hardcoded Wiring
records.intent: Replace enumerated wiring with convention-based discovery, so new components register without editing a central list.
records.invariant: Components are discovered by convention at runtime; no central switch enumerates each one.

records.title: Declarative Config Over Imperative
records.intent: Replace imperative setup steps with declarative configuration describing the desired state.
records.invariant: Configuration declares the target state; it is not a sequence of mutation calls.

records.title: Anti-Corruption Layer Over Cross-Context Leak
records.intent: Insert an anti-corruption layer at a context boundary, so a foreign model cannot corrupt the local one.
records.invariant: A foreign model is translated at the boundary; its shape never leaks into the local bounded context.

records.title: Injected Nondeterminism Over Hidden
records.intent: Inject clocks, randomness, and IO so the core is deterministic and testable, isolating nondeterminism at the edge.
records.invariant: Sources of nondeterminism are injected; the core computes deterministically given its inputs.

records.title: Pattern By Fit Over Speculative Pattern
records.intent: Introduce a pattern only when a present force demands it, avoiding accidental complexity from anticipated needs.
records.invariant: Every abstraction traces to a current force; none exists solely for a hypothesized future.
